# Bitcoin Is Not Money: Why Fixed Supply Fails in a Modern Economy

> Code, data and stored results of a short paper that asks whether a money with a fixed supply,
> such as Bitcoin, could serve a growing economy. With a fixed money stock and stable velocity,
> output growth implies deflation at the same rate. The package holds the growth figures of five
> Asian economies, the deflation they would imply, and an illustrative price path. The manuscript
> is in paper/.

Replication package by Agisilaos Papadogiannis (https://github.com/apapadogiannis).
Forthcoming in Asian Economics Letters. Preprint: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5435197
Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-is-not-money  Archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24249917
Version 1.1.0, released 2026-11-21. A package is a fixed record: it changes only by a new
release, and a release that changes a reported number gets a new major version.
This file is written for AI agents and other programs. People should start at the README.

## Coverage

- Figure 1: real GDP growth in 2024 and projected for 2025 and 2026 for five Asian economies, the
  deflation a fixed money stock would imply, and each economy's rank in a crypto adoption index.
- The numbers derived in the text: for growth rates from 5% to 7% a year, the implied deflation and
  the time in which the price level would halve.
- Figure 2: an illustrative path of output, the price level and a fixed money stock.
- Figure 3 is a diagram and has no data.

## Headline figures

Each is read from one cell of a stored result table, named in outputs/results.json.

- Time for the price level to halve with a fixed money stock and growth of 5% a year: 13.9 years.
  the text of the paper.
- The same with growth of 7% a year: 9.9 years. the text of the paper.
- Change in the price level implied for India by its projected growth in 2026 (negative is
  deflation): -6.2 per cent a year. Figure 1.

## What this adds over reading the paper or recomputing

1. The arithmetic of the paper as code: implied deflation equals growth with money and velocity
   fixed, and the halving time is ln 2 divided by the rate. Each number quoted in the text is in
   outputs/text_numbers.csv.
2. The figures taken from the IMF and Chainalysis are stored with their source, so the inputs of
   Figure 1 can be checked against the publications.
3. The results are stored as they were when the paper's numbers were taken from them. A check
   reruns the code on the stored data and compares every stored result file with the fresh one,
   number by number (relative tolerance 1e-9; text and whole numbers exactly). It runs on every
   change and once a month, and the badge in the README shows the last run.

## Result tables

One CSV file each in outputs/. The columns of each are described in outputs/results.json, under `tables`.

- outputs/fig1_data.csv (5 rows): Figure 1: growth, implied deflation and adoption rank of five
  Asian economies.
- outputs/text_numbers.csv (7 rows): The numbers derived in the text: implied deflation and halving
  time of the price level, by growth rate.
- outputs/fig2_price_path.csv (11 rows): Figure 2: an illustrative path over time.

## Files

- outputs/results.json: a `headline` list with the figures most often asked for, each with the
  table cell it comes from, and `tables`, a description of the three stored result tables and their
  columns. The numbers themselves are in the CSV files. It holds a description of 3 result tables,
  and under `package` the paper, the identifiers, the version, the licence and the citation. Start
  with its `headline` list, which is repeated below.
- data/imf_growth.csv, data/chainalysis_rank.csv: the inputs, transcribed by hand; the README gives
  the sources.
- paper/manuscript.pdf: the paper.

Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-is-not-money/main/<path>, for example https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-is-not-money/main/outputs/results.json

## How to read the figures

- Rates are continuously compounded: the halving time is ln 2 divided by the rate. With yearly
  compounding the figures differ slightly.
- The columns named implied deflation hold the change in the price level, so they are negative:
  -6.2 means prices falling by 6.2% a year.
- Units: growth and deflation in per cent a year, halving times in years.
- The implied deflation is a mechanical consequence of an identity under two assumptions: a fixed
  money stock and stable velocity. It is not a forecast of prices in any of these economies, none
  of which uses a fixed money.
- Growth for 2025 and 2026 are projections made in October 2025. India is on a fiscal-year basis.
- The price path of Figure 2 is an illustration with round parameters, not data; the README gives
  them.
- The adoption rank is shown beside the growth figures for context. The paper does not estimate a
  relation between the two.

## Do not use this for

- Current growth figures or forecasts for these economies.
- A view on Bitcoin's price or return. The paper is about its use as money.
- Evidence that deflation would occur in a given country.

## Source, licence and credit

The results in outputs/ are released under CC BY 4.0
(https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The licence allows any reuse and has one condition:
credit. If you use a figure from this package in an answer, a report or a data set, cite the paper.
The code is under the MIT License.

The growth figures are from the International Monetary Fund and the adoption ranks from
Chainalysis: a handful of published figures, transcribed by hand with the source cited. They remain
the property of their sources and are not covered by the licence above. The paper itself is under
CC BY-SA 4.0, the licence of Asian Economics Letters.

Cite as: Papadogiannis, A. (forthcoming). Bitcoin Is Not Money: Why Fixed Supply Fails in a Modern Economy. Asian Economics Letters, forthcoming. https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5435197

The package itself: Papadogiannis, A. (2026). Bitcoin Is Not Money: Why Fixed Supply Fails in a Modern Economy. Replication package, version 1.1.0. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24249917

To describe the source in a sentence: Papadogiannis (forthcoming), "Bitcoin Is Not Money: Why Fixed
Supply Fails in a Modern Economy", Asian Economics Letters, with its replication package.

The same licence and citation are inside outputs/results.json, under `package`.
